migrationAliasesNote: Maps a key a host config actually carries to the canonical server id. Prune keeps only what the canonical set names after Resolve-McpAliasKey, so an unaliased drifted key is deleted rather than reconciled. Recorded 2026-08-19: .claude/settings.json carried repowise-workspace under the key 'repowise', and migrationAliases was empty, so a prune run would have removed the only working repowise registration on the machine. Verified the canonical args are safe to converge on: 'repowise mcp' defaults to stdio, so the deployed '--transport stdio' is redundant and dropping it changes nothing.

rules: Prefer a shared remote endpoint over a locally spawned process.
A local server runs as one process shared across agents; multiple hosts must not each spawn their own instance of the same server.
A local server is started by the plugin or skill that needs it, not eagerly at session start, so no process is running for a session that never uses it.
activationPolicy.note: Recorded from an explicit owner preference on 2026-08-04: local MCP processes were multiplying across hosts and costing CPU and memory for sessions that never invoked them. activationMode carries this per server. 'shared-remote' means the fleet talks to one hosted endpoint and starts nothing locally. 'on-demand-local' means a local process is permitted, but only invoked through an owning capability, and only when that capability is used. A local server that would be eagerly started by every host at session start does not satisfy this policy regardless of how its activationMode reads.

hostInventory.note: Which hosts actually exist on this machine, established 2026-08-19 by enumerating ~/.local/bin, ~/bin, %APPDATA%/npm(+node_modules), %LOCALAPPDATA%/Programs, Program Files, Program Files (x86), WindowsApps, %LOCALAPPDATA%/Packages, WinGet Links/Packages, the uninstall registry, and the VS Code / VS Code Insiders / Cursor extension dirs. The field is named 'hosts' so Test-RegistryHostReferences.ps1, which validates every property literally named 'hosts' against agents.json, checks these ids too. notInstalled entries are checked-and-absent, not unchecked: hermes has ~/AppData/Local/hermes with skills but no binary anywhere (its ~/bin/hermes-acp.cmd shim points at a venv path that does not exist), and windsurf has ~/.codeium/windsurf config but no binary and no host extension. An on-demand-local server must not name either -- see Test-LocalMcpHostScope.ps1.

protocolRevisionNote: Every server carries a `protocol` block establishing which MCP revision it actually speaks, probed rather than assumed. This exists because `transport: "http"` stopped being informative once the 2026-07-28 revision made the core stateless: a 2025-11-25 server and a 2026-07-28 server are both 'http' and are not wire-compatible. `revision: null` is a legitimate recorded state meaning 'could not be established', and it must say why -- it is never a placeholder for an unchecked entry. Known revisions are listed in knownProtocolRevisions.

mcpServers.name: Playwright MCP (headed, per-workspace profile)
mcpServers.providesCapabilitiesNote: The fleet's browser layer, replacing chrome-devtools on 2026-08-19. Headed by default -- verified the same day by driving it to https://example.com and observing a real window titled 'Example Domain - Google Chrome for Testing', so the owner can watch and take over a run. Chosen over chrome-devtools for one decisive reason: chrome-devtools' persistent profile lives at a single path under $HOME, and Chrome permits one browser per user-data-dir, so fanning it across hosts on this one workstation means the first host to open a browser takes the lock and every other host fails at launch. Playwright partitions its profile as mcp-{channel}-{workspace-hash}, so per-host processes cannot collide. Cost is also far lower than the appium precedent: measured 10-22 MB per daemon here versus appium's ~93 MB per host. Serves browser.isolated natively; browser.authenticated via --storage-state or a signed-in workspace profile, without ever touching the owner's personal Chrome. For parallel or CI runs use --isolated, or one HTTP server (--port) that hosts dial by URL, where each client gets its own context by default.

localProcessPolicy.note: Pinned @playwright/mcp@0.0.79. Unlike a single-shared-process server this is safe per host, because Playwright derives its profile directory from the workspace hash, so two host sessions never contend for one directory. localProcessPolicy.launchNote: Declared as npx for portability, but Sync-AgentHub's Resolve-WindowsHiddenStdioEntry resolves it to the global install and runs %APPDATA%/npm/node_modules/@playwright/mcp/cli.js under node.exe directly, preserving the --browser flag. This corrects an earlier claim that these hosts cold-fetched the package on every session start: the global install already prevented any fetch, so what npx still cost was npm's own CLI bootstrap. Measured 2026-08-20, identical handshake both ways (protocolVersion 2025-11-25, serverInfo Playwright 1.63.0-alpha-2026-08-05): 2.12s to MCP initialize through npx-cli.js against 0.48s launching cli.js directly. That 1.64s was paid once per host session on each of the eight hosts. tests/Test-McpLauncherDirectness.ps1 now asserts that no deployed entry boots npm to reach a package already installed globally; playwright was the last server on the fleet still doing so.
